newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude positive, gasoline weak.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude positive, gasoline weak.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were expected to open higher on Monday but gasoline still looks weak and this is casting a bearish shadow over the market, traders and brokers said.

August NYMEX crude oil, the new front month, closed three cents a barrel down on Friday at $18.89 a barrel while heating oil was 0.12 cents a gallon down at 51.33 cents. July gasoline was 0.61 cents down at 55.48 cents.
"Part of the weakness on Friday stemmed from the expiration of the July contract," said Victor Yu at Refco in New York. "With July off the board it is looking a bit more positive."
He saw key resistance for August at $19.24 a barrel. This corresponds to previous days' highs. Above this level, he said, lay resistance at $19.62.
He said he saw support for August crude at $18.78-$18.80. "The market is pretty much bound up in this range."
But gasoline, he said, was looking less healthy. "Gasoline is not looking particularly good."
He saw psychological support for the market at 55 cents a gallon and the most important resistance at 58.35 cents.
"But I think we are going to test the lower numbers. As soon as gasoline goes I think the rest of the market will go with it."
MeesPierson Derivatives in London said that following the break on Friday of recent range lows, they expected more falls.
"Preparation is negative across the board, leading us to look for rallies to sell," Fenella Graham said in her daily report.
Employing her company's Market Profile chart technique, she said of August crude oil: "We continue to sell rallies to $19.16."
"A break lower and we join, waiting for a buying extreme to take profits. A move above 19.16 and we cut any shorts, waiting for a move up to $19.52 to sell again."
Sher also pegged support for July gasoline at 55 cents, and saw resistance up at 56.40 and 57.10 cents a gallon.
